understanding and usage of basic instruments and software
present and discuss concepts and information, in oral or written way
basic study organization, day-by-day, and to make mid-term plans
basic ability to identify and use links between phenomena, their properties and their representations

learning_outcomes.text: After the completion of this teaching activity, the student should know and understand: each module of a system for signal processing and transmission; how to evaluate its performance. The student will also know the basic methods to design a system for signal processing and transmission.

After the completion of this teaching activity, the student should be able to: evaluate the performance of a system for signal processing and transmission against given requirements and operating constraints; identify each module in order to design a global system that satisfy the requirements; chose the best technologies in order to design each module.
The student will be able to evaluate the design process and results.

After the completion of this teaching activity, the student should be able to explain in an organic way the dependences among the different modules of a signal processing and transmission system, and the dependences of these modules on the device where they have been deployed.

The student will be able to follow and understand the technology updates, understand the technical documentation, and to integrate all different information in order to have a broad view of problems and solutions relevant to signal processing and transmission systems.

assessment_methods.method: final assessment written exam on Signal Theory topics

assessment_rules: Each student is evaluated by weekly assessment tests (2 points per week) and a final assessment written exam on Signal Theory topics, and by an optional oral exam. For the intermediate assessment, the score is given by weighting the answers to different exercises. All these assessments contribute to reach the final mark; 32 points or more are necessary to achieve a “30 e lode” mark. If the final exam mark is not sufficient (i.e. 18 or more), the student should ask for an oral assessment.
